name: Louisiana

agency.name: Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (LDEQ)
agency.division: Office of Environmental Services, Air Permits Division

overview: In Louisiana any source that emits or could emit an air contaminant generally needs an air permit unless an exception applies. Very small facilities are excused by statute (Act 547) or can use the small source exemption (LAC 33:III.501.B.4); insignificant activities are listed in LAC 33:III.501.B.5. Other non-Part 70 facilities get state minor source permits under LAC 33:III.503, or coverage under minor source general permits such as the one for crude oil and natural gas production. Major sources need Part 70 (Title V) permits under LAC 33:III.507, plus PSD or nonattainment NSR for major projects.

permitTypes.name: No permit required (Act 547 / R.S. 30:2054(B)(2)(b)(ix))
permitTypes.description: Facilities with facility-wide potential emissions below the limits generally need no permit; before exceeding them, apply for a permit or small source exemption. Portable source emissions count totals from all sites.
permitTypes.thresholds: Per LDEQ: below 5 TPY of each regulated pollutant, below 15 TPY combined, and below the minimum emission rate (MER) for each toxic air pollutant.
permitTypes.quote: facility-wide potential emissions are less than five tons per year for each of any regulated air pollutant as defined by the Clean Air Act, 42 U.S.C. 7401 et seq., less than fifteen tons per year emitted of all such defined pollutants combined

quoteSource.name: LDEQ: Do I Need an Air Permit? (Act 547 text)

permitTypes.name: Small Source Exemption
permitTypes.description: For sources that are not major sources, with low criteria pollutant emissions, toxic air pollutants below the minimum emission rate (MER) in LAC 33:III.5112, Table 51.1, no need for enforceable permit conditions, and no public notice required. The source must operate under the terms of the exemption.
permitTypes.thresholds: No more than 5 tons per year of any criteria pollutant, and less than the MER in LAC 33:III.5112, Table 51.1, for each Louisiana toxic air pollutant (LAC 33:III.501.B.4.a). LDEQ's web page words the first test as any regulated pollutant.
permitTypes.quote: the source emits and has the potential to emit no more than 5 tons per year of any criteria pollutant

permitTypes.name: Insignificant Activities
permitTypes.description: Listed activities exempt from permitting based on size, pollutant, and activity; case-by-case claims under 501.B.5.D.

permitTypes.name: Regulatory permits (LAC 33:III Chapter 3)
permitTypes.description: Notification-based permits for listed sources and activities, including oil and gas well testing, release of natural gas from pipelines, stationary internal combustion engines, storage vessels, boilers and process heaters, and stationary combustion turbines. Sources not covered by a regulatory permit are permitted under Chapter 5.
permitTypes.quote: Regulatory permits may be used to authorize emissions of air contaminants as defined in LAC 33:III.111 from the sources and activities identified in this Chapter by notifying the department of the planned activity using the appropriate form provided by the department.

quoteSource.name: Louisiana Administrative Code, Title 33, Part III (Office of the State Register)

permitTypes.name: Minor Source General Permits
permitTypes.description: General permits for numerous similar sources, including crude oil and natural gas production facilities.
permitTypes.quote: The permitting authority may issue a general permit intended to cover numerous similar sources or activities.

quoteSource.name: Louisiana Administrative Code, Title 33, Part III (Office of the State Register)

permitTypes.name: State (Minor Source) Permit
permitTypes.description: For facilities that are not Part 70 sources. LAC 33:III.503.B lists three routes: an exemption under 501.B.4, a small source permit, or coverage under a general permit issued under 513.A. Minor source permits have a ten-year term, and renewal applications are due at least 6 months before expiration (503.C). Fees are under LAC 33:III Chapter 2.
permitTypes.thresholds: Small source permit: less than 25 tons per year of any criteria pollutant and 10 tons per year of any toxic air pollutant (LAC 33:III.503.B.2).
permitTypes.quote: Small Source Permit. The owner or operator of a stationary source which is not a part 70 source may apply for a small source permit provided the source emits and has the potential to emit less than 25 tons per year of any criteria pollutant and 10 tons per year of any toxic air pollutant.

permitTypes.name: PSD
permitTypes.description: Major source review in attainment areas under LAC 33:III Chapter 5.
permitTypes.quote: The requirements of this Section apply to the construction of any new major stationary source, as defined in Subsection B of this Section, or any project at an existing major stationary source in an area designated as attainment or unclassifiable under Sections 107(d)(1)(A)(ii) or (iii) of the Clean Air Act.

quoteSource.name: Louisiana Administrative Code, Title 33, Part III (Office of the State Register)

permitTypes.name: Nonattainment New Source Review
permitTypes.description: Major source review in nonattainment areas under LAC 33:III Chapter 5. Section 504 is titled Nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR) Procedures and Offset Requirements in Specified Parishes.

permitTypes.name: Part 70 (Title V) Operating Permit
permitTypes.description: For major sources; Title V general permits also exist.
permitTypes.citation: LAC 33:III.507; major source defined in LAC 33:III.502
permitTypes.quote: Major Source— for the purposes of determining the applicability of 40 CFR part 70 or of LAC 33:III.507, any stationary source or any group of stationary sources that are located on one or more contiguous or adjacent properties, that are under common control of the same person (or persons under common control) that belong to a single major industrial grouping

oilAndGas.summary: Louisiana has a minor source general permit for crude oil and natural gas production facilities (SIC 1311) and midstream gas compression and processing (SIC 1389), with lower facility-wide limits in the five-parish Baton Rouge area. Part 70 sources and some others are excluded.

programs.name: Minor Source General Permit: Crude Oil and Natural Gas Production Facilities
programs.description: Covers field production and midstream compression/processing below facility-wide limits. Excludes Part 70 sources and facilities subject to LAC 33:III Chapter 59 or 40 CFR Part 68, among others.
programs.thresholds: Per LDEQ general permit (facility-wide PTE, tpy): Baton Rouge area (Ascension, East Baton Rouge, Iberville, Livingston, West Baton Rouge): PM10 15, SO2 40, NOx 20, CO 90, VOC 20, total TAPs 20, individual TAP 8. Other parishes: same except NOx 90 and VOC 90.
